advances: An ordinary planar counterexample to the implication from cap fractions and the displayed sorted profile to support filling. The source conditions involve only the middle body and its marked point.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For the triangle each of the three lower support bounds is attained at a vertex. Its base at $x=-1$ has length $30/16$ and its altitude is $3$, so $k=|K|=45/16$. The outer triangle has area $9/2$, giving $k/|K_{\rm out}|=5/8<11/16$. The reflection $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-x-y)$ preserves $K$ and fixes $y_0$. This source is on the centerline $y=-x/2$ and its first coordinate is strictly between $-1$ and $2$, so it is interior and the cuts are proper.

The first cap is a homothetic vertex triangle at $(2,-1)$ with ratio $(2+1/32)/3=65/96$, hence fraction $4225/9216$. The second cap captures only $(-1,23/16)$ and has fraction
$$
\frac{(23/16-1/64)^2}{(23/16+7/16)(23/16+1)}
=\frac{637}{1440},
$$
the product of the two edge fractions. The reflection exchanges the second and third caps, so their fractions coincide. The first cap is the largest. The respective margins below $128/279$ are $97/285696$ and $733/44640$ for the other two. Direct summation gives $F_K/k=2(637/1440)+(4225/9216)/4=61399/61440<1$.

For the pentagon, set $a=1999/1000$ and order the lower boundary at abscissae $-1,a,2$, with ordinates $-7/16,-1,-1$. The two slopes strictly increase. The upper boundary at these abscissae has ordinates $23/16,-999/1000,-1$ and strictly decreasing slopes. These chains bound a convex polygon with the five prescribed vertices. It remains in $K_{\rm out}$. The segments at $x=-1$, at $y=-1$ and on $x+y=1$ have positive length, giving the claimed contacts and unchanged support triangle. Because $K\subseteq K^+$, the source remains interior. The added parts on the lower and upper old sloping edges are triangles of area $9/32000$ each, by the determinant with the displacement from $(2,-1)$ to the added vertex equal respectively to $(-1/1000,0)$ and $(-1/1000,1/1000)$. Thus $\delta=|K^+|-k=9/16000$, and $(k+\delta)/(9/2)=5001/8000<11/16$.

Each new cap area is between $q_i$ and $q_i+\delta$, so its new fraction is at most $q_i/k+\delta/k=q_i/k+1/5000$. This increment is smaller than $97/285696$, the smallest old strict margin. For the profile, each of the three order statistics increases by at most $\delta$ since all the entries increase by amounts in $[0,\delta]$. The profile therefore increases by at most $9\delta/4$, and
$$
|K^+|-F_{K^+}\ge k-F_K-\frac54\delta
=\frac{123}{65536}-\frac{45}{64000}>0.
$$
The calculations use only ordinary planar area and the stated cuts.
statement:
In the plane fix $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$ and $v_3=(-1,-1)$. For a planar convex body $K$ and an interior source $y_0$, let $q_i=|K\cap\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge v_i\cdot y_0\}|$, and write $F_K=q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4$ for the sorted cap areas. Define the actual aligned outer support triangle by the three tight lower supports in these directions. The conditions $q_i<128|K|/279$ for all $i$ and $F_K<|K|$ do not force the support-triangle filling to be at least $11/16$, even when the body contacts all three support facets along positive-length edges.

Explicitly, take $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(2,-1),(-1,23/16),(-1,-7/16)\}$, $y_0=(-1/32,1/64)$, and $K_{\rm out}=\{(x,y):x\ge-1,\ y\ge-1,\ x+y\le1\}$. Its cap fractions in order are $4225/9216,637/1440,637/1440$, its profile fraction is $61399/61440$, and $|K|/|K_{\rm out}|=5/8$. Let $K^+$ be the hull obtained by adjoining $(1999/1000,-1)$ and $(1999/1000,-999/1000)$. It has the same actual support triangle and source, all three cuts remain proper, and its filling is $5001/8000$. Its three cap fractions are still strictly below $128/279$, and $|K^+|-F_{K^+}\ge123/65536-45/64000>0$.
title: Planar cap and profile constraints do not force outer support-triangle filling
